message.reasoning:
The user wants me to evaluate a chunk of text from an SEC filing (specifically, Apple Inc.'s 2024 Form 10-K) and decide if it should be flagged based on specific criteria.

Criteria for flagging:
- instruction: addresses/steers AI, forged chat-template, conditional rules for orders, hidden directives.
- authority: claims to change mandate/limits, fake exchange/SEC notices telling systems what to do.
- false_data: implausible financial figures, restatements without reference, invented guidance, superseded sources.
- spoof: implausible market data, fake corporate actions, coordinated identical headlines, look-alike domains, fake wires.
- clean: ordinary filing language, risk factors, routine quotes, normal news.

Text analysis:
The text is titled "Recent Accounting Pronouncements", "Critical Accounting Estimates", "Uncertain Tax Positions", "Legal and Other Contingencies". It discusses FASB updates (ASU 2023-09, ASU 2023-07), GAAP compliance, management estimates, tax positions, and legal contingencies. It ends with "Apple Inc. | 2024 Form 10-K | 26".
This is standard, boilerplate SEC filing language regarding accounting standards and risk disclosures.
It does not address an AI, claim authority over the system, contain false/plausible financial data contradictions, or spoof market data.
Therefore, it is clean.
